public_rationale: The retrieved evidence points toward continued development in the months after publication. The Seoul commitments concern conditional responses to particular risks, rather than an implemented broad pause. No decisive contradiction was verified. However, assigning a closing date to “near-term” would add a commitment Marcus did not make, so the forecast cannot receive a final supported score under the stated horizon rules.
limitations: The main contemporaneous account comes from the organization advocating the pause.
US federal legislative evidence does not establish worldwide absence.
A fixed one-year or two-year interpretation could change whether the forecast is treated as elapsed.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: There will be no moratorium on AI development in the near term.

statement.excerpt: We are obviously never going to have a moratorium anytime in the near-term.
statement.document_title: Six months after the Pause letter, AI is still erratic — and still something we should still be deeply concerned about

from_speaker: never going to have a moratorium
our_interpretation: In the pause-letter context, a moratorium means a broad government-imposed or industry-wide pause in frontier-model development.
Restrictions on particular uses, local data-center construction, and pauses on AI regulation do not constitute that moratorium.
“Near-term” supplies no duration from which a latest date can be calculated. No six-month, one-year, or two-year deadline is added.
The forecast therefore remains open for formal scoring, although evidence from the months following publication can bear on its direction.
criteria.support_condition: Reliable records establish that no qualifying moratorium occurred throughout a bounded near-term period grounded in the speaker’s wording or contemporaneous clarification.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A broad frontier-development moratorium was adopted during a period unambiguously within the forecast’s near-term scope.
